t:
(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 500 East Whitestone Boulevard in Cedar Park, Texas, shall be known and designated as the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”.

fable.w: This section only names a Postal Service facility and says existing references to it are deemed to use the new name. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but it appears only in boilerplate about existing records and authorizes no new rule. No state, tribe, expert, member of the public or other outside party is consulted, heard or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference

qwen_block.w: This section simply designates a name for a federal facility and updates references to that facility. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.

(a) Designation.—The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 500 East Whitestone Boulevard in Cedar Park, Texas, shall be known and designated as the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”.

opus.w: This section only names a post office and says that existing references to the facility mean the new name. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The word "regulation" is just one item in a list of records, not a grant of rulemaking authority, so it does not count as participation.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning:** The tempting reading is to treat the word "regulation" as if it gave rulemaking authority, which would count as participation. That reading fails. The word only appears in a list of documents whose references to the post office are deemed to refer to its new name. Nothing here authorizes a regulation, a hearing, a consultation or an advisory body. It also brings in no one outside the federal government. The section simply names a building.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a name for a federal facility. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this decision. The action is a unilateral legislative act.
qwen_chat.s: The facility of the United States Postal Service located at 500 East Whitestone Boulevard in Cedar Park, Texas, shall be known and designated as the “Army Specialist Matthew Troy Morris Post Office Building”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after a specific person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision to name the building. It is a unilateral legislative designation.
